newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Nizhny Novgorod area eyes March 97 Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: Russia Nizhny Novgorod area eyes March 97 Eurobond.

text.p: Russia's Nizhny Novgorod region may issue a three-year Eurobond of up to $50 million in March 1997 but does not plan any short-term Treasury bill issues, a senior regional official said on Thursday.
Yuri Podlesov, head of securities at the regional oblast administration's finance department, said ING Barings would finish assessing the region's credit-rating by next March.
"Then, in March, we will begin our Eurobond issue on Western markets," he said.

He said Nizhny Novgorod region, home to the reform-minded city of the same name, was not interested in the state-sponsored, rouble-denominated short-term debt market, whose high-yield papers are known as GKOs.
Nizhny Novgorod region is home to the GAZ autoworks, the Norsi oil refinery, Svyazinform Nizhny Novgorod and has pilot agriculture privatisation programmes.

A handful of Russian regions and cities, including Moscow, St Petersburg and Sverdlovsk, are planning Eurobonds after Russia's $1 billion Eurobond was oversubscribed this month and established a borrowing benchmark for other Russian entities.
